she
he
they

my
their
his

rationales.our: Our would include me as a person sharing the room, contrary to the context.
rationales.my: My would make the room mine alone instead of the guests'.
rationales.his: His changes a two-person possession into one man's possession.

findings: Original Luis notice-board sentence reused the timetable frame and offered no plural ownership contrast.

Let's stop proposes a shared action, so suggests a rest captures its purpose.

offered to carry my case
refused to carry my case

rationales.offered to carry my case: Offered to carry reports the passenger's volunteered help with my case.

items.setupText: Choose the natural pattern with 'told' and a named listener.

told that
told to us that
told us to that

rationales.told us that: 'Told us that' names the listeners and introduces the information they received.

findings: Original Yara pair-practice item repeated one sentence with no distinction between reporting-verb complements.

items.setupText: A guide says, 'The river runs through the city.' The report begins with 'says', not 'said'.

options: run through the city
running through the city
is run through the city
runs through the city

rationales.run through the city: 'Run' lacks the singular -s required with the river in this present statement.
rationales.running through the city: 'Running' needs an auxiliary to form a complete verb phrase here.

rationales.where I had parked: Where I had parked keeps indirect-question order and the requested past-perfect verb.

rationales.who the flowers had ordered: This makes the flowers the subject of 'ordered' instead of keeping 'who' as the subject.

rationales.who had ordered the flowers: 'Who' is the subject of 'had ordered', so no separate subject or do-support is needed.

rationales.had lost her membership card: Had lost provides the requested past perfect, and her keeps the card as the member's.

rationales.had already left: Had already left remains past perfect; no extra had is added merely because it is reported.

had to bring our own tools

rationales.had to bring our own tools: Had to bring reports the obligation applying to us at that past time without saying whether we complied.

items.setupText: The steward said, 'You may use the side entrance.' Choose the report of the permission given to us.

rationales.had used the side entrance: Had used reports an action as completed instead of granting permission.
rationales.had to use the side entrance: Had to turns an available option into a requirement.
rationales.were allowed to use the side entrance: Were allowed to reports may as permission without making the action compulsory or completed.

confirmed that we had checked our tires
advised us to check our tires
asked us whether we had checked our tires
items.answer: advised us to check our tires
items.explanation: Advised us to preserves the recommendation expressed by should.

rationales.ordered us to check our tires: Ordered makes the speech stronger than the stated advice.
rationales.confirmed that we had checked our tires: Confirmed asserts completed checking instead of recommending it.
rationales.asked us whether we had checked our tire: Asked whether turns advice into a request for information about an earlier check.

findings: Original Jonas bookstore-in-email item gave a repeated place question without any calibrated reporting verb.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves the strength and purpose of a recommendation.

items.setupText: We were deciding how to travel. My sister said, 'Let's take the train.' Complete the suggestion report.

us to take the train

taking the train
items.answer: taking the train
items.explanation: Suggested taking uses the -ing complement to report the proposed shared action.

rationales.to take the train: Suggest does not take a to-infinitive directly in this pattern.
rationales.taking the train: Suggested taking uses the -ing complement to report the proposed shared action.
rationales.us to take the train: Suggest does not use the object-plus-to pattern of advise us to take.
rationales.that taking the train: That needs a complete clause, such as that we take the train, not just taking the train.

findings: Original Priya laboratory item repeated where the place was rather than testing a reporting-verb complement.
audit.microSkill: Suggested plus -ing for a shared proposal
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes suggest taking from advise someone to take.
audit.levelReason: A common travel suggestion provides focused B1 complement-pattern practice.

items.setupText: The seller told me, 'I promise I'll replace the damaged mug.' Keep the replacement as the seller's commitment.

options: promised that I would replace the damaged mug
asked me to replace the damaged mug
promised to replace the damaged mug
said I had promised to replace the mug
items.answer: promised to replace the damaged mug
items.explanation: Promised to replace keeps the seller as the person committed to replacing the mug.

rationales.promised that I would replace the damage: This makes the customer's replacement action the content of the promise, instead of keeping the seller responsible.
rationales.asked me to replace the damaged mug: Asked me shifts the replacement action to the customer and changes a promise into a request.
rationales.promised to replace the damaged mug: Promised to replace keeps the seller as the person committed to replacing the mug.
rationales.said I had promised to replace the mug: This attributes the promise to me rather than to the seller.

findings: Original Kenji community-center sentence repeated the same question pattern with a handbook tail.
audit.microSkill: Speaker commitment retained under promise plus to-infinitive
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps the person responsible for a promised action distinct from its recipient.
audit.levelReason: Reporting a clear everyday promise with correct role assignment is B1 work.
audit.similarityNote: A replacement promise rather than volunteered luggage help or a listener-directed request.

items.setupText: A neighbor said, 'Be careful. The stream may flood tonight.' Choose a report keeping the warning and its uncertainty.
items.taskText: Our neighbor ___.
options: promised that the stream would flood tonight
warned us that the stream might flood tonight
confirmed that the stream had flooded
warned us that the stream could not flood
items.answer: warned us that the stream might flood tonight
items.explanation: Warned us preserves the caution, and might keeps flooding as possible rather than certain.

rationales.promised that the stream would flood ton: Promised misrepresents a caution as a commitment, and would removes the original may possibility.
rationales.confirmed that the stream had flooded: Confirmed ... had flooded turns a possible future danger into an established past event.
rationales.warned us that the stream could not floo: Could not flood denies the danger rather than warning that it is possible.
rationales.warned us that the stream might flood to: Warned us preserves the caution, and might keeps flooding as possible rather than certain.

findings: Original Sara garden-after-policy-reminder item had no meaningful caution despite its appended policy context.

audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps both the speech function and the speaker's limited certainty.
audit.levelReason: An everyday weather warning with might is appropriate B1 reporting work.

items.setupText: The guest said, 'I'm sorry I arrived late.' Complete the apology report.
items.taskText: The guest apologized ___.
options: to arrive late
for arriving late
that arriving late
for arrive late
items.answer: for arriving late
items.explanation: Apologized for takes an -ing phrase naming the action the guest regrets.

rationales.for arriving late: Apologized for takes an -ing phrase naming the action the guest regrets.
rationales.to arrive late: To arrive would not give the normal complement naming the reason for this apology.
rationales.that arriving late: That arriving is not a complete clause and does not fit this apology pattern.
rationales.for arrive late: After for, use arriving rather than the base form arrive.

findings: Original Luis market-support-call sentence recycled question-order foils with generic explanations.
audit.microSkill: Apologize for plus -ing to report regret for an action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Reports an apology through its conventional preposition and action complement.
audit.levelReason: A short, familiar social apology suits B1 complement practice.

items.setupText: The musician was asked to sign a poster and answered, 'No, I won't sign it.' Choose the report of that response.

options: denied signing the poster
offered to sign the poster
refused to sign the poster
asked whether the poster was signed
items.answer: refused to sign the poster
items.explanation: Refused to sign reports the unwillingness to perform the action requested.

rationales.denied signing the poster: Denied signing would reject a claim that signing happened, not refuse a requested future action.
rationales.refused to sign the poster: Refused to sign reports the unwillingness to perform the action requested.
rationales.offered to sign the poster: Offered would show willingness instead of the expressed refusal.
rationales.asked whether the poster was signed: Asked whether would seek information about the poster rather than reject the request.

findings: Original Emma workshop-training sentence repeated the place-location template without any response to report.
audit.microSkill: Refusal of an action distinguished from denial of a past action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates won't do it from didn't do it when selecting a reporting verb.
audit.levelReason: A clear request-and-response context supports B1 speech-function discrimination.

items.setupText: It is still the same week. On Monday a colleague said, 'The exhibition ends this week.' Compare two reports made on Wednesday.
items.taskText: A: 'She said the exhibition ended this week.' B: 'She said the exhibition ended that week.'
options: Both can refer to the same week in this context.
A must be wrong because this always changes to that after said.
B must mean a week later than the exhibition's final week.
A means the exhibition has already ended, while B means it has not.
items.answer: Both can refer to the same week in this context.
items.explanation: The shared week allows this week, while that week can refer back to the week being reported.

rationales.A must be wrong because this always chan: This week can remain accurate when the original speaker and the reporter are within the same week.
rationales.B must mean a week later than the exhibi: That week can point back to the week of the original statement; it does not automatically mean a later week.
rationales.Both can refer to the same week in this: The shared week allows this week, while that week can refer back to the week being reported.
rationales.A means the exhibition has already ended: This versus that does not by itself establish whether the ending has already happened at Wednesday's reporting time.

findings: Original Noah reception-desk sentence mixed a past question with a present filing tail and gave blanket correctness claims.
audit.microSkill: Time demonstrative retained when the reporting week is unchanged
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids applying this-to-that replacement mechanically when both references are accurate.
audit.levelReason: A clear same-week context makes reporting-time flexibility teachable at B1.
audit.similarityNote: Accepts two contextually valid time phrases instead of repeating the A2 day-shift exercises.

items.setupText: Choose what the sentence establishes, without treating the manager's message as independent proof.
items.taskText: The manager said that the coffee machine was broken.
options: The sentence reports the manager's statement that it was broken.
The sentence proves that the machine was broken.
The sentence says the manager broke the machine.
The sentence says the manager was unsure whether it was broken.
items.answer: The sentence reports the manager's statement that it was broken.
items.explanation: The sentence attributes the broken-machine claim to the manager without independently establishing it.

rationales.The sentence proves that the machine was: Reporting what someone said does not itself provide independent proof of the content.
rationales.The sentence says the manager broke the: The manager is the speaker, not an identified cause of the fault.
rationales.The sentence says the manager was unsure: The reported statement contains no uncertainty such as might or perhaps.
rationales.The sentence reports the manager's state: The sentence attributes the broken-machine claim to the manager without independently establishing it.

findings: Original Yara classroom-checklist item only tested a recurring grammatical frame and never distinguished speech from evidence.
audit.microSkill: A reported statement distinguished from independent confirmation
audit.pedagogicalValue: Introduces the basic limit of what said that commits the reporter to.
audit.levelReason: A short everyday message makes source attribution accessible at B1 before later layered reports.
audit.similarityNote: A simple speech-versus-proof distinction, not a passive reporting or nested allegation exercise.

items.setupText: Leah tells Victor, 'I'll send you my recipe.' Choose Victor's report, preserving both people and the recipe's owner.
items.taskText: Victor says: 'Leah told me that ___.'
options: I would send her my recipe
she would send him my recipe
he would send me her recipe
she would send me her recipe
items.answer: she would send me her recipe
items.explanation: She refers to Leah, me to Victor as reporter, and her recipe remains Leah's recipe.

rationales.she would send me her recipe: She refers to Leah, me to Victor as reporter, and her recipe remains Leah's recipe.
rationales.I would send her my recipe: This makes Victor the sender and recipe owner, reversing the original roles.
rationales.she would send him my recipe: Him fails to keep Victor's first-person reporting viewpoint, and my changes the owner to Victor.
rationales.he would send me her recipe: He changes the sender from Leah to a male person not identified as the original sender.

findings: Original Theo cafeteria-after-tutor item finished twenty largely identical where-be questions with boilerplate feedback.
audit.microSkill: Speaker, recipient, and possessive coordinated in a listener's report
audit.pedagogicalValue: Tracks three person references together while preserving a future commitment.
audit.levelReason: Coordinating several pronoun changes in a short practical message is B1 reporting work.
audit.similarityNote: A recipe sent between two named people; the names appear only in this relationship-focused item.

items.setupText: Choose the interpretation that does not treat backshift alone as evidence of a later change.
items.taskText: The technician said that the casing was waterproof. No later test is mentioned.
options: The past was proves that the casing is no longer waterproof.
Was can reflect the past reporting viewpoint; it does not establish a later loss of waterproofing.
The sentence independently confirms that the casing is still waterproof now.
The technician said that the casing had stopped being waterproof before she spoke.
items.answer: Was can reflect the past reporting viewpoint; it does not establish a later loss of waterproofing.
items.explanation: Was can locate the reported property at the speaking time without saying whether it has since changed.

rationales.The past was proves that the casing is n: Backshift after said does not itself imply that the reported property has ceased.
rationales.Was can reflect the past reporting viewp: Was can locate the reported property at the speaking time without saying whether it has since changed.
rationales.The sentence independently confirms that: The sentence reports the technician's statement and does not independently verify a current property.
rationales.The technician said that the casing had: Was waterproof reports the property, not its ending before the conversation.

findings: Original audit-file meeting item claimed to report a quote that was not supplied and tested only would plus base form.
audit.microSkill: Backshift distinguished from a claim that a property ended
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids inferring present falsity merely from a past verb in reported speech.
audit.levelReason: Interpreting what backshift does and does not imply is B2 reporting control.
audit.similarityNote: A product property whose later status remains open, not an A2 state known to have changed.

items.setupText: Choose what the report says without adding an outcome.
items.taskText: The curator announced that the gallery would reopen after the repairs.
options: The repairs were complete when the announcement was made.
The gallery certainly reopened, although the announcement date is unknown.
Reopening was presented as later than the repairs; the report does not confirm that it happened.
The gallery was already open when the curator announced the repair plan.
items.answer: Reopening was presented as later than the repairs; the report does not confirm that it happened.
items.explanation: The report presents the reopening prospectively and keeps the after-repairs sequence without confirming fulfillment.

rationales.The repairs were complete when the annou: After the repairs sets the condition or sequence for reopening; it does not establish completion at announcement time.
rationales.The gallery certainly reopened, although: Would reopen reports a future event from a past viewpoint, not a verified later outcome.
rationales.Reopening was presented as later than th: The report presents the reopening prospectively and keeps the after-repairs sequence without confirming fulfillment.
rationales.The gallery was already open when the cu: Was already open reverses the future orientation of would reopen.

findings: Original policy-review meeting sentence repeated would start at noon with elementary malformed alternatives.
audit.microSkill: Reported future announcement separated from fulfillment
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes an announced future event from evidence that the event later took place.
audit.levelReason: Reading future-in-the-past and its limits is B2 interpretation.
audit.similarityNote: A gallery announcement with a repair condition, not another promised phone call.

items.setupText: Report 'How long have you been waiting?' using a past-perfect continuous clause in standard written order.
items.taskText: The dispatcher asked us ___.
options: how long we had been waiting
how long had we been waiting
how long we had being waiting
how long we have been waiting
items.answer: how long we had been waiting
items.explanation: We had been waiting preserves the duration question with embedded order and the requested aspect.

rationales.how long had we been waiting: Had we is direct-question inversion; the indirect clause requires we had.
rationales.how long we had being waiting: Had must be followed by been, not being, in the perfect continuous.
rationales.how long we have been waiting: Have been waiting can be used in some current reports, but the instruction specifically requires past perfect continuous.
rationales.how long we had been waiting: We had been waiting preserves the duration question with embedded order and the requested aspect.

findings: Original Aiko budget-meeting item only varied a meeting tail and used the same would-start key.
audit.microSkill: Duration question reported with past-perfect continuous and embedded order
audit.pedagogicalValue: Keeps an accumulated ongoing activity intact while reporting its duration question.
audit.levelReason: Coordinating duration, aspect, and indirect syntax is B2 form control.
audit.similarityNote: Duration of waiting, extending rather than duplicating B1 simple perfect questions.

items.setupText: The host asked me, 'Who invited you?' Choose the report keeping the unknown person as the inviter.
items.taskText: The host asked ___.
options: whom I had invited
who I had sent an invitation to
who had invited me
whether I had invited anyone
items.answer: who had invited me
items.explanation: Who is the inviter, and me remains the person who received the invitation.

rationales.who had invited me: Who is the inviter, and me remains the person who received the invitation.
rationales.whom I had invited: This makes me the inviter and asks for the person I invited, reversing the original roles.
rationales.who I had sent an invitation to: Sending an invitation also makes me the inviter rather than the recipient.
rationales.whether I had invited anyone: This changes a who question about my inviter into a yes/no question about my own invitations.

findings: Original Nadia manager-briefing sentence offered no participant-role discrimination beyond a repeated future form.
audit.microSkill: Subject versus object roles in grammatical reported who questions
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes who invited me from whom I invited without relying on malformed foils.
audit.levelReason: Choosing among grammatical indirect questions by role and question type suits B2.
audit.similarityNote: An invitation's direction, not the B1 formal assembly of a subject-who perfect question.

items.setupText: Choose the linker used before a to-infinitive when reporting a choice in standard written English.
items.taskText: The tenants discussed ___ to renew the lease or move elsewhere.
options: if
that
what
whether
items.answer: whether
items.explanation: Whether to renew introduces the choice between renewal and moving.

rationales.if: If does not normally introduce a to-infinitive choice in this standard written construction.
rationales.whether: Whether to renew introduces the choice between renewal and moving.
rationales.that: That introduces a finite content clause, not this choice followed by a to-infinitive.
rationales.what: What would ask which thing to renew, whereas the sentence asks whether renewal should happen.

findings: Original Omar complaint-review item repeated a scheduled meeting with no meaningful reporting complement.
audit.microSkill: Whether plus to-infinitive for a reported deliberation
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes an infinitival choice construction from finite if questions.
audit.levelReason: The complement restriction and explicit alternatives are appropriate B2 grammar.
audit.similarityNote: A tenants' deliberation uses an infinitival question rather than a tense-shifted finite question.

items.setupText: The customer asserted a right to immediate repayment: 'I insist that you refund me now.' Choose the report preserving that force.
items.taskText: The customer ___.
options: suggested that a refund might be useful
wondered whether a refund was available
demanded an immediate refund
offered to refund the payment
items.answer: demanded an immediate refund
items.explanation: Demanded captures the explicit insistence, and immediate preserves now.

rationales.suggested that a refund might be useful: Suggested ... might be useful weakens the insistence into a tentative proposal.
rationales.wondered whether a refund was available: Wondered whether turns an asserted demand into uncertainty about availability.
rationales.demanded an immediate refund: Demanded captures the explicit insistence, and immediate preserves now.
rationales.offered to refund the payment: Offered to refund makes the customer the person returning money rather than requesting it.

findings: Original Lena data-check item reused would start with no calibration of reporting-verb force.
audit.microSkill: Explicit insistence reported without weakening its force
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves the difference between a demand, a suggestion, an inquiry, and an offer.
audit.levelReason: Matching a reporting verb to the strength of a supplied utterance suits B2.
audit.similarityNote: A direct refund demand contrasts with the seller's promise and the cycling advice.

items.setupText: A passenger said to the driver, 'You ignored my stop.' Complete a report attributing that accusation to the passenger.
items.taskText: The passenger accused the driver ___.
options: to ignore the stop
for ignoring the stop
that he ignored the stop
of ignoring the stop
items.answer: of ignoring the stop
items.explanation: Accused the driver of ignoring names the person blamed and the alleged action without confirming the accusation.

rationales.to ignore the stop: Accuse someone does not take a to-infinitive for the alleged act in this construction.
rationales.for ignoring the stop: The conventional preposition after accused the driver is of, not for.
rationales.that he ignored the stop: A that clause cannot directly replace the of-phrase after accused the driver here.
rationales.of ignoring the stop: Accused the driver of ignoring names the person blamed and the alleged action without confirming the accusation.

findings: Original Sofia training-portal meeting item used only basic modal agreement errors as B2 distractors.
audit.microSkill: Accuse a person of an -ing action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Reports blame through the appropriate complement without adopting it as verified fact.
audit.levelReason: A less elementary reporting-verb pattern with an alleged action suits B2.
audit.similarityNote: An accusation about a missed stop, not a refusal to perform a future action.

items.setupText: The coach said to the runners, 'Well done on finishing your first marathon!' Complete the congratulation report.

options: for to finish their first marathon
on finishing their first marathon
to finish their first marathon
that finishing their first marathon
items.answer: on finishing their first marathon
items.explanation: Congratulated them on finishing reports praise for the achievement already completed.

rationales.on finishing their first marathon: Congratulated them on finishing reports praise for the achievement already completed.
rationales.for to finish their first marathon: For to finish incorrectly combines a preposition and to-infinitive in this compliment pattern.
rationales.to finish their first marathon: To finish sounds like an intended action, but congratulate does not take this direct infinitive complement.
rationales.that finishing their first marathon: That finishing is not a complete content clause and does not fit this pattern.

findings: Original Daniel contract-signing tail mixed time frames while repeating elementary would-start grammar.
audit.microSkill: Congratulate a person on an achieved action
audit.pedagogicalValue: Reports praise for an achievement using the appropriate -ing complement and possessive.
audit.levelReason: A conventional reporting pattern beyond say and tell is suitable B2 work.
audit.similarityNote: Positive acknowledgment of a completed marathon, distinct from an apology or accusation.

items.setupText: Choose the comparison keeping a proposed action distinct from an assertion about the past.
items.taskText: A: 'She insisted on paying the bill.' B: 'She insisted that she had paid the bill.'
options: Both report her assertion that payment had already happened.
A reports her determination to pay; B reports her firm claim of earlier payment.
A reports a demand that someone else pay; B reports her own refusal to pay.
Both independently prove that she paid the bill.
items.answer: A reports her determination to pay; B reports her firm claim of earlier payment.
items.explanation: On paying presents her insistence on the action, whereas that she had paid supplies the content of an assertion about earlier payment.

rationales.Both report her assertion that payment h: Only B explicitly reports the claim that payment had already occurred; A concerns insisting on doing it.
rationales.A reports her determination to pay; B re: On paying presents her insistence on the action, whereas that she had paid supplies the content of an assertion about earlier payment.
rationales.A reports a demand that someone else pay: She is the intended payer in A, and B asserts payment rather than refusing it.
rationales.Both independently prove that she paid t: Neither the insistence on an action nor the report of a claim independently proves the payment outcome.

findings: Original Rina customer-update item repeated a future meeting without distinguishing meanings of a reporting verb.
audit.microSkill: Action insistence versus factual insistence distinguished by complement
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids conflating a determination to act with a firm assertion that one acted.
audit.levelReason: Comparing two grammatical insist constructions by speech function suits B2.
audit.similarityNote: One bill supports a genuine complement-and-meaning contrast rather than two contextual variants.

items.setupText: The electrician reassured the residents: 'The supply is safe.' Choose the report of reassurance, not a claim that he carried out safety work.
items.taskText: The electrician ___.
options: ensured that the supply was safe
assured the residents that the supply was safe
made the supply safe for the residents
required the residents to make the supply safe
items.answer: assured the residents that the supply was safe
items.explanation: Assured the residents reports reassurance addressed to people while retaining its stated content.

rationales.ensured that the supply was safe: Ensured says he made certain of safety; it does not specifically report reassuring speech to the residents.
rationales.made the supply safe for the residents: Made the supply safe asserts an intervention that the quoted reassurance does not establish.
rationales.assured the residents that the supply wa: Assured the residents reports reassurance addressed to people while retaining its stated content.
rationales.required the residents to make the suppl: Required ... to make changes reassurance into an instruction assigning safety work to residents.

findings: Original Mateo planning-call item provided no actual call content and repeated would plus base form.
audit.microSkill: Assure a listener distinguished from ensure an outcome
audit.pedagogicalValue: Separates reassurance through speech from making an outcome happen or checking it.
audit.levelReason: Discriminating closely related reporting and action verbs is B2 lexical-grammatical control.
audit.similarityNote: An electrician's reassurance, not a promise of future repairs.

items.setupText: Choose the report that leaves the existence of a fault open, as the original question does.
items.taskText: The engineer asked, 'Is the sensor faulty?'
options: The engineer asked why the sensor was faulty.
The engineer explained that the sensor was faulty.
The engineer asked when the sensor had become faulty.
The engineer asked whether the sensor was faulty.
items.answer: The engineer asked whether the sensor was faulty.
items.explanation: Whether preserves the open question of whether a fault exists.

rationales.The engineer asked why the sensor was fa: Why treats a fault as the basis for asking its cause, rather than asking whether there is a fault.
rationales.The engineer explained that the sensor w: Explained that reports a statement about a fault instead of a yes/no inquiry.
rationales.The engineer asked when the sensor had b: When asks for the onset of a fault and treats becoming faulty as given.
rationales.The engineer asked whether the sensor wa: Whether preserves the open question of whether a fault exists.

findings: Original Hana hiring-process meeting sentence had no real question or uncertainty to preserve.
audit.microSkill: Open yes/no inquiry distinguished from a presupposing wh-question
audit.pedagogicalValue: Avoids importing an assumed fault while reporting an inquiry about possible malfunction.
audit.levelReason: Choosing among grammatical reports by their background assumptions is B2 reading and editing.
audit.similarityNote: Sensor status remains open; this is not merely selection of the linker if.

items.setupText: The librarian said, 'You ought to keep a record of your sources.' Keep 'ought to' unchanged in the report.
items.taskText: The librarian said that we ___.

ought kept a record of our sources
had ought to keep a record of our sources
would ought to keep a record of our sources
items.answer: ought to keep a record of our sources
items.explanation: 'Ought to' is retained, with the base form 'keep', while 'our' adjusts the possessive to the reporting group.

rationales.ought to keep a record of our sources: 'Ought to' is retained, with the base form 'keep', while 'our' adjusts the possessive to the reporting group.
rationales.ought kept a record of our sources: 'Ought' needs 'to' plus the base verb here, not the past form 'kept'.
rationales.had ought to keep a record of our source: 'Had' cannot be added as a backshift auxiliary before 'ought' in this standard construction.
rationales.would ought to keep a record of our sour: 'Would' cannot be stacked before 'ought' to make the intended report.

findings: Original Jonas project-dashboard item reused elementary future backshift as its only B2 demand.
audit.microSkill: Ought to retained without stacking reporting auxiliaries
audit.pedagogicalValue: Shows a limit to mechanical modal backshift while preserving a recommendation.
audit.levelReason: A less frequent modal and its unchanged reported form suit B2 consolidation.
audit.similarityNote: A source-recording recommendation with ought to, not another should-to-advised paraphrase.

items.setupText: A resident says angrily, 'The drilling starts before dawn every day.' Choose a report of the complaint without adding an order or a remedy.
items.taskText: The resident ___.
options: ordered the builders to finish before dawn
promised to stop the drilling before dawn
asked what time the drilling started
complained that the drilling started before dawn each day
items.answer: complained that the drilling started before dawn each day
items.explanation: Complained preserves the angry statement and its repeated early starting time.

rationales.ordered the builders to finish before da: The resident states a grievance about starting time, not an instruction about finishing time.
rationales.complained that the drilling started bef: Complained preserves the angry statement and its repeated early starting time.
rationales.promised to stop the drilling before daw: A promise to stop the work adds both a commitment and control over the work that the source does not state.
rationales.asked what time the drilling started: The resident already states the time; the utterance is not an information question.

findings: Original Priya board-discussion meeting item ignored communicative purpose and recycled malformed future verbs.
audit.microSkill: Complaint reported without inventing a requested remedy
audit.pedagogicalValue: Preserves a speaker's grievance while avoiding unsupported commands or promises.
audit.levelReason: Using context to select a reporting verb and limit its added meaning is B2 work.
audit.similarityNote: A neighborhood noise grievance, separate from a refund demand with an explicit requested remedy.

items.setupText: A friend recommends a cheaper route: 'Why don't you go by coach?' Choose a report of that recommendation, not a literal question about past reasons.

denied that I could go by coach
confirmed that I had gone by coach
items.answer: suggested that I go by coach
items.explanation: Suggested that I go preserves the recommendation made through the conventional why-don't-you form.

rationales.denied that I could go by coach: Denied that I could rejects an option that the friend is recommending.
rationales.suggested that I go by coach: Suggested that I go preserves the recommendation made through the conventional why-don't-you form.
rationales.confirmed that I had gone by coach: Confirmed ... had gone reports a completed journey, not a proposed choice.

findings: Original Kenji revised-procedure item supplied no direct utterance and tested only a repeated future pattern.
audit.microSkill: Why-don't-you recommendation distinguished from literal why inquiry
audit.pedagogicalValue: Uses the supplied purpose to preserve advice conveyed through question form.

items.setupText: The equipment clerk said, 'Don't forget to return your helmet.' Choose the report of a reminder about a pending action.

remembered returning my helmet
asked why I had returned my helmet
reminded me to return my helmet
items.answer: reminded me to return my helmet
items.explanation: Reminded me to return keeps me as the person who still needs to carry out the action.

rationales.remembered returning my helmet: Remembered returning makes the clerk the person recalling an action rather than someone reminding me to act.
rationales.asked why I had returned my helmet: Asked why seeks a reason for an earlier return rather than prompting a pending return.
rationales.reminded me to return my helmet: Reminded me to return keeps me as the person who still needs to carry out the action.

findings: Original Sara service-report tail changed only context around the repeated meeting sentence.
audit.microSkill: Prospective remind-to complement versus retrospective that-clause
audit.pedagogicalValue: Distinguishes prompting someone to do something from recalling that it has been done.

items.setupText: An editor wants to characterize the original conditional. What does the surviving report allow the editor to conclude?

options: The report preserves an originally remote left/would conditional.
The original condition could have been open or more hypothetical.
The report backshifts an original leave/will conditional.
The report treats the guests' departure as an established event.

items.setupText: What does this sentence establish about the result of the mediation?

The mediator established that the plan was workable because both teams sincerely endorsed it.
The mediator reported that both teams had privately believed the plan workable before the discussion.
The mediator secured public statements; the teams' private convictions remain unspecified.

items.explanation: Persuaded them to state concerns a successful action commitment; it does not establish sincere acceptance of the statement's content.

items.setupText: Which summary accurately captures the architect's correction?
items.taskText: The architect said, 'I called the design "unprecedented", not "unacceptable".' No further evaluation was given.
options: The architect denied finding the design unacceptable.
The architect corrected the word attributed to her, without settling whether she considered the design acceptable.
The architect withdrew a judgment that the design was unprecedented and endorsed it as acceptable.
The architect admitted disapproving of the design but preferred a less direct expression.
items.answer: The architect corrected the word attributed to her, without settling whether she considered the design acceptable.
items.explanation: The contrast corrects which description she used; 'unprecedented' does not itself mean 'acceptable' or 'unacceptable'.

rationales.The architect corrected the word attribu: The contrast corrects which description she used; 'unprecedented' does not itself mean 'acceptable' or 'unacceptable'.
rationales.The architect withdrew a judgment that t: She maintains 'unprecedented' as her wording and supplies no endorsement of acceptability.

items.setupText: Which conclusion follows from this sentence?
items.taskText: Not all the witnesses denied seeing the cyclist.
options: There was at least one non-denial, which need not have been an admission.
Some witnesses admitted seeing the cyclist.
None of the witnesses denied seeing the cyclist.
At least one witness saw the cyclist, whether or not that witness admitted it.
items.answer: There was at least one non-denial, which need not have been an admission.
items.explanation: Negating all requires at least one non-denial but does not identify the person's response as an admission.

rationales.Some witnesses admitted seeing the cycli: Failure to deny can include silence or another response; it does not necessarily constitute an admission.
rationales.None of the witnesses denied seeing the: Not all leaves open that some witnesses did deny it, so none is stronger than the source.

items.setupText: How does the narrator present the newsletter's account?

The narrator's conclusion about withdrawal is conditional on accepting the newsletter's account.
The narrator confirms withdrawal and merely doubts the newsletter's explanation for it.
The newsletter makes its own accuracy conditional on whether the choir withdraws.

items.setupText: Which report of the director's position is justified?
items.taskText: The director said, 'My objection is not to those remarks themselves, but to your making them in front of the clients.'
options: The director criticized the audience choice without settling the remarks' truth.
The director denied the remarks' truth because clients had heard them.
The director endorsed the remarks as true but wanted the clients to believe something different.
The director objected to anyone making the remarks in any setting, including before clients.
items.answer: The director criticized the audience choice without settling the remarks' truth.
items.explanation: The contrast places the objection on the public audience; absence of an objection to the remarks themselves does not settle their truth.
